Application Materials.content:
You will need to provide the following documentation as part of your application. This list of documents may vary slightly from course to course.
- **Academic qualifications:** Please provide a transcript for your degree study. If you have not yet completed your degree please provide a transcript of your results achieved to date. If you have completed more than one university qualification, please provide a transcript and certificate for both.
- If your degree was awarded by a UK university, please upload a transcript of your marks for each year or an electronic Higher Education Achievement Reports (HEAR).
- If your degree was awarded by an overseas institution, you should supply a transcript of your marks for each year of your studies and a copy of your degree certificate together with a certified translation if the document is not in English. International and EU applicants are also advised to include high school transcripts.
- We accept copies of physical transcripts and degree certificates as well as electronic transcripts and certificates. Please **do not** submit originals of certificates or transcripts by post.
- If you are submitting copies of physical documents, you should upload to your application clear, colour photographs or scans of your original qualification documents (not copies or certified copies). These documents must confirm that the qualification has been awarded, show the date of the award, and show the final awarded grade.
- **Referee details:** Please provide the contact details of one or two referees on your application as required. You should provide details of an academic referee if you are currently studying, or if you have graduated within the last five years. Professional references may be considered if you have graduated more than five years ago.
- Open references will normally only be accepted if they are written on headed paper, provided as a colour copy of the original, and provide the referee’s work contact details. If you have open references, please upload these at the time of application.
- If you do not have open reference, Queen Mary will contact your referee(s) via email to supply a reference, preferably electronically. References by email can only be accepted if sent from a university or company email address; references from a personal email address such as 'Yahoo' or 'Hotmail' are not acceptable.
- Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company stamp or on official institution/company letterhead, and should be provided as a scanned colour copy of the original.
- **Statement of purpose:** Your statement of purpose should explain why you want to study your chosen programme and how it will help your future career aspirations. This should typically be one side of A4 paper.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV)/Resume**
- **English language certificate (if applicable):** If English is not your first language, you should provide evidence of English language ability: IELTS, TOEFL, or other acceptable proof.
You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **No background in mathematics required.** Applications are invited from **all disciplines**.
- UK degree requirement: **A 2:2 or above at undergraduate level in any subject**.
- For applicants from China: Queen Mary normally considers **Bachelor Degree (minimum 4 years) from selected institutions** for entry to postgraduate taught programmes. For a UK 2:2 degree equivalency, the requirement is **65 to 75%**; offer conditions will vary depending on the institution you are applying from.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English language requirements for entry to postgraduate taught and research programmes in the School of Mathematics falls within the following English band: **Band 4: IELTS (Academic) minimum score 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking**.
Queen Mary accepts a range of English tests and qualifications categorised in English bands to demonstrate English Language proficiency. See [all accepted English tests](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/accepted-english-language-tests-and-qualifications/) deemed equivalent to these IELTS scores.

Program Overview.content:
During a time of great global uncertainty, particularly in the areas of climate change, health and regulation, many organisations are looking for risk managers who have both traditional risk management knowledge and data analysis skills to solve the problems presented in the world today. This programme provides students with a comprehensive grounding in risk management, including risk analytics, data analytics and the application of statistics in risk management. Within second semester elective modules, students will have the opportunity to specialise in certain areas of risk management such as risk regulation, and sustainability and climate risk.
- Become highly employable in a variety of industries including finance, medicine, IT, science, technology, and regulatory bodies, where risk management professionals are in high demand.
- Learn real-world key risk management knowledge in areas affecting our world today.
- Opportunities to take elective modules in areas such as risk regulation and sustainability and climate risk.
This programme is designed for students who want a career in risk regulation across the globe. With such a large number of industries requiring risk management professionals, students who graduate from this programme will have the skills and knowledge to work in a wide range of industries including finance, medicine, IT, science, technology and regulatory bodies.

Curriculum.content:
Study options for Risk Analytics MSc include **Full-time, September 2026 | 1 year**, **Part-time, September 2026 | 2 years**, and **Full-time, September 2027 | 1 year**. Location: **Mile End**.
- Semester One: students focus on compulsory modules providing foundations for a risk-related career, covering fundamental risk analytics tools, statistics, data analytics, machine learning, and key risk management theories in Enterprise Risk Management and Finance.
- Semester Two: students choose all modules and tailor the programme to interests, career plans or professional background. Elective modules allow specialisation in areas such as Enterprise risk analytics (with Actuarial Risk Management 2), Financial risk analytics (with Digital and Real Asset Analytics and Financial Data Analytics), Sustainability and Climate Risk Analytics, and Regulatory Risk Analytics.
- Semester Three: students work on a dissertation, developing hands-on skills for industries, government agencies, or academic institutions.
Structure:
- Four compulsory modules
- Four elective modules (chosen from 7)
- Final project and dissertation
Compulsory/Core modules:
- Actuarial Risk Management 1
- Foundations of Mathematics and Statistics
- Risk Analytics Dissertation: each Risk Analytics MSc student is required to complete a **60 credit project dissertation**. A student must find a potential supervisor and fill out a Risk Analytics MSc Project Approval Form by the end of Semester B. The supervisor and project must be approved by the Risk Analytics MSc Programme Director. A typical MSc project dissertation consists of about 30 pages, covering a specific research-level topic in Risk Analytics, usually requiring the student to apply risk management tools to measure, predict, or manage certain types of risks. An MSc project may also involve collaboration with a collaborator based in industry.
- Financial Instruments and Markets
- Data Analytics
Elective modules:
- Regulatory Risk Analytics
- Optimisation for Business Processes
- SAS for Business Intelligence
- Digital and Real Asset Analytics
- Computational Statistics with R
- Actuarial Risk Management 2
Assessment:
- 67% Modules
- 33%
- Students are assessed by a mixture of formal examinations and coursework in taught modules.
- Students complete a substantial Risk Analytics Project with strong industrial relevance, focusing on practical applications, professional skills, and the latest developments at the frontier of the field.
Teaching is primarily through a combination of lectures and tutorials, in addition to independent study and research.

Financial Aid.content: Queen Mary is pleased to offer a number of generous scholarships to students on our MSc programmes. A wide range of other scholarships and bursaries are available, including the [Queen Mary Alumni Loyalty Award](http://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/funding_masters/queen-mary-alumni-loyalty-award/) and the UK government's international [Chevening Awards](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/chevening-awards.html). **Find out about all scholarships and bursaries available to Queen Mary postgraduate applicants [here](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/funding_masters/).** If you have any questions about Scholarships available to applicants within the School of Mathematical Sciences, please contact [maths@qmul.ac.uk](mailto:maths@qmul.ac.uk).

Multiple Applications.content:
You may apply for a **maximum of two taught programmes** or **one taught and one research programme** at Queen Mary per application cycle. Please note that you can only study for one qualification at a time, so if you receive offers for both programmes you will be required to accept one and decline the other.
No, the university does not charge an application fee.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: If you wish to defer or withdraw your application, you can do this via the [Applicant Portal](https://mysis.qmul.ac.uk/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_lgn). Simply click on "Request a change" and follow the instructions. Please note you **must have met the academic requirements in order to defer your place**.
